Everything here is running in development. Production has not been moved yet.

The archive jobs existed only to manage the size of the database.

Our own apps are MoreCast, fire watch and the climatology page. They read the station data directly. From the weather model grids, the API gives the forecast at one place. Reading all of BC needs the library. No app reads the grids yet.

The five models are HRDPS, RDPS and GDPS (Canadian), GFS (American) and ECMWF (European).

11,722 rows. The climatology page goes further, and compares this year with every other year, day by day.

Kamloops, 50.70, -120.44. Times are UTC.

Delta Lake was not chosen for speed. Plain Parquet was faster in our test, and Delta Lake needs nightly upkeep. The test used made-up data for 300 stations over 60 days, on a local disk. File counts carry over to object storage. Read times don't. Zarr was 36% smaller for observations. It was still about three times as many files as our two arrangements together, and the best at neither read. Postgres was not in the test, so there is no fair comparison of speed with the old database. The files cut to BC were estimated, not built. Our evaluation did not cover Iceberg or TimescaleDB.

Replacing A and B with D is what the nightly compaction does: many small files become one. No data changes. Each file is at least one request to storage, so many small files make a read slower. The replaced files are kept for 30 days, so a table can be read as it was at any point in that time. Two jobs can't write the same log entry. The second one has to try again or fail. Each table has its own log, so a write to two tables is two separate steps.

The picture is not to scale, and the line is only an illustration. A block is 64 by 64 grid cells with every forecast hour. There is one for each variable. Reading all of BC for one hour means reading every block, which is why that takes longer.

This is the development address. It works from any language that can make a web request.

60 requests a minute for each key.

Deployed to development on November 24. It has been tested locally, and not yet checked there. The values are from the nearest grid cell, and the response says where that is. A place outside BC is an error, and so is a run that isn't kept.

Set SUFFIX first. Without it the library uses production's location.

The ideas are not planned work.

The database check was MoreCast's model read in development on November 16, over 14 days. 0.0 is to one decimal, for the same run.

This is the weather data only. MoreCast's own data stays in Postgres, so that cluster and its backups stay, but the cluster no longer has to hold weather history. The weather model jobs no longer use the database at all. The upkeep jobs compact and clean up the files, and rebuild the by-station tables. The files' speed has not been compared fairly with the database's.

Production still uses the old system until it is moved. Once it is, object storage being down would affect MoreCast and fire watch as well as the API and the climatology page. Icechunk is open source too, but it is newer and less widely used than Delta Lake and Zarr. Our Postgres backups were kept in object storage anyway, so we already relied on it. The storage is Dell ECS, run by the OCIO. If one data centre is unavailable, it fails over to the other. Mirroring is constant but asynchronous, so the newest writes may not have been copied yet. Mirroring does not undo a mistake, because a deletion is mirrored too. A Delta table can be read as it was for 30 days, which covers a mistake inside a table. It does not cover losing the bucket. Rebuilding needs the original records, so it does not cover losing those. Two jobs writing one table at once is only partly tested. We haven't run it long enough to say it is more stable. On November 23 the HRDPS grid store stopped accepting data for about 12 hours and we don't know why. Station model jobs also ran out of memory while publishing, which has been fixed. The original records are the model runs and the WF1 observations and forecasts. They are added to and never replaced.

This is for the weather model grids only. It does not include the station data.

MoreCast and fire watch should work as before. The old database tables stay until production's history has been copied and checked.
